titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 24/2014 (ސްޕެޝަލް އިކޮނޮމިކް ޒޯންގެ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް ... ވަނަ އިސްލާހު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This government bill amends the Special Economic Zone Act (Law No. 24/2014) to create a new type of zone called a "sustainable township" (new Article 17-1). A sustainable township is a residential area under one management, with mixed-use real estate and/or integrated tourism, plus homes, services and public facilities. A new chapter (Articles 70-1 and 70-2) says a permit is only given if the investment is at least US$500 million and the zone includes luxury tourism or luxury housing, an international hospitality training centre or health centre, at least 60% renewable energy, and food production facilities. It sets a fixed list of tax breaks for these zones, including a 5% business income tax for the first 10 years, and adds a freehold transfer tax on long-term strata leases of villas and rooms (Article 22-1).
whyItMatters: Developers investing US$500 million or more could build large resort-style towns where villas and rooms are sold or leased long term, paying lower taxes than normal for up to 20 years. People who buy villas or rooms in these zones would pay a transfer tax through the seller.
keyProvisions: Article 17-1 defines a "sustainable township" and Article 20 adds it as a new zone type (20(v)); Article 9 is updated to cover zone types up to Article 17-1.
Article 22-1 adds a freehold transfer tax of 4% on long-term strata leases of villas or rooms in a zone, collected by the seller from the buyer and paid to the Maldives Inland Revenue Authority.

Article 70-1 lists permit conditions: at least US$500,000,000 invested, a luxury integrated tourism or mixed-use development, an international hospitality training centre or health centre, at least 60% of the zone's energy from renewables, and farming or aquaculture facilities.

Article 70-2 says these zones get only the benefits listed there: freehold transfer tax of 1%, then 2%, then 4% for later periods; business income tax of 5% for years 1 to 10, 10% for years 11 to 20, and the normal Income Tax Act (Law No. 25/2019) rate from year 21.

Article 70-2 also exempts developers from income tax on profits from selling residential villas or rooms, and exempts imported capital goods for building the zone from import duty; the general benefits under Article 23 do not apply.

Article 82 adds definitions of luxury real estate and luxury integrated tourism developments (each at least US$500 million); Article 79 updates references to the Foreign Investment Act (Law No. 11/2024) and the Income Tax Act (Law No. 25/2019); regulations are due within 6 months.
whoIsAffected: Large investors and developers, buyers or long-term leaseholders of villas and rooms in these zones, and the Maldives Inland Revenue Authority.
statedReasons: The explanatory note says the government is proposing the bill to allow special economic zones to be set up as sustainable townships, and to set the conditions and rules for those zones.
